literal: And meanness, and lingering discontent, and poverty, if they are absent, the army will conquer.
translation: If an army is free from meanness, lingering discontent, and poverty, it will achieve victory.
modern: சிறுமைக்குணம், நீங்காத வெறுப்பு, வறுமை ஆகியவை இல்லாதிருந்தால், அந்தப் படை வெற்றி பெறும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the three internal defects that can ruin an army, regardless of its size or weapons. First is 'ciṟumai' (meanness or smallness of spirit), which refers to a lack of courage or noble character. Second is 'cellāத் tuṉi' (lingering discontent or resentment), which represents internal discord or grievances against the ruler that do not go away. Third is 'vaṟumai' (poverty or deprivation), which saps the soldiers' strength and morale. If an army is free from these three flaws, it is guaranteed to win.
